**Bill Timeline:** *This vote happens during the main debate on the bill's core principles. A second reading amendment does not change the actual text of the proposed law. Instead, it amends the motion itself and is used by politicians to express an opinion about the bill, highlight perceived flaws, or call for further action.*

At 12:39 PM, a large majority voted against a second reading amendment introduced by Independent MP [Priya Nakamura](https://www.theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/fairview/priya_nakamura) (Independent) to the [Consumer Data Right Amendment (Portability) Bill 2026](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/bills/consumer-data-right-amendment-portability-bill-2026), which means it was unsuccessful. Because the amendment sought to decline the bill a second reading, a vote for it was in effect a vote against the bill proceeding.

Nobody voted against their party on this occasion.

### About the Bill

> No Bill Digest found.

### About the Amendment

At 12:39 PM, Independent MP Priya Nakamura states that this amendment will:

> * Noting that many small retailers do not yet have the systems needed to comply with the bill's proposed timeframe.
>
> * Arguing consumers should be given more time before new data-sharing obligations begin.
>
> * Warning the bill would add compliance costs for regional businesses without any support package.

### Amendment Text

> That all words after "whilst" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:
>
> "declining to give the bill a second reading, the House also notes that:
>
> (1) many small retailers still lack the technical systems needed to comply with the proposed timeframe;
>
> (2) consumers should be given a longer transition period before new data-sharing obligations take effect; and
>
> (3) the bill, in its current form, would place additional compliance costs on regional businesses without a corresponding support package".
